relevance_note: Single case report of a man with nephrotic syndrome, cloudy cornea and very low HDL whose renal biopsy findings were 'suggestive of LCAT deficiency', i.e. a clinical/histological (not genetic) diagnosis of LCAT deficiency.
method_note: Read the paper by hand; output assembled with a short Python script in the scratch directory, every value from my own reading. One in-scope person (the single unnamed patient, label 'patient'). No genetic testing and no plasma LCAT activity are reported, so no LCAT variant is tied to him: the variants table is empty, and n_patients_reported is null because the paper states no number of patients with an LCAT variant (in scope via a clinical/histological diagnosis of LCAT deficiency). Siblings ('youngest of three children. No other members in the family were affected') are not described individually and get no rows. Age 28 is the age at presentation; the last reported evaluation is the 1-year follow-up, whose age is not stated, so age_at_last_evaluation uses the presentation age. Lipid values printed without a label (LDL 59 mg/dl, triglycerides 253 mg/dl, VLDL 51 mg/dl, total cholesterol 122 mg/dl) were not turned into checklist statuses; low LDL and hypertriglyceridemia are 'not reported'. Low HDL is observed from 'very low serum HDL' (Discussion) with the value. 'Tubulo interstitial compartment and blood vessels were normal' is a whole-compartment normal finding: recorded as excluded 'abnormal tubulo interstitial compartment' only; the checklist item 'tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis' is left 'not reported' (D-27). Normal respiratory/cardiovascular/nervous examinations recorded as written; atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease left 'not reported'. 'Hemolytic anemia ... not seen in our patient' excludes hemolytic anemia only; the broader checklist item 'anemia' is left 'not reported'. Serum creatinine 1.1 mg/dl and 'stable renal functions' do not state normal renal function, so CKD/renal failure is 'not reported'. Immunofluorescence 'insignificant mesangial deposits of IgM and C3c' not recorded as a feature. Vital status not explicitly stated. No contradictions found.

consanguinity.span: He was born of nonconsanguinous marriage

treatment_summary.value: ramipril 10 mg/day, with partial remission of proteinuria at 1-year follow-up; glasses for blurred/diminished vision
span: The patient was started on ramipril 10 mg/day.
There was partial remission of proteinuria with stable renal functions at 1-year follow-up.
He complained of blurring of vision, which was rectified by glasses.
The patient has diminished vision and is using glasses.

clinical_diagnosis_basis.value: clinical and renal histology (light and electron microscopy); no genetic testing or LCAT activity measurement reported
span: Electron microscopy showed diffuse effacement of podocyte foot processes, capillary loop and mesangial regions were distended by electron lucent lipid material containing electron dense proteinaceous matrix suggestive of LCAT deficiency.
the combination of nephrotic syndrome, cloudy cornea, foam cells with lipid deposits in glomeruli and very low serum HDL are typical of complete LCAT deficiency
